title: PHD2 cannot be configured during onboarding unless PHD2 is already running
summary: The onboarding guider step only wrote the guider into the draft inside `if (running)` after a successful socket probe, so a user setting up indoors before launching PHD2 could not record a guider at all - Next dropped the typed host/port and the summary step read '- not set -'. Added an explicit 'Use PHD2' action (plus 'Clear') that persists the draft guider and the phd2Host/phd2Port settings the connect path reads, independent of the probe; Test stays as verification and still selects in one tap when it passes. The selection line is now derived from the draft (not a local flag), so picking a native guider retires it.

title: FocusModelPanel is orphaned - the machine that builds the temperature-compensation model cannot display it
summary: Confirmed: `FocusModelPanel` was constructed nowhere, and Imaging -> Focus carried only Manual Focus and Autofocus, so an operator running autofocus on that very screen had no view of the model those runs build (Settings' focus-model page is remote-only). Mounted the maintained, backend-aware `FocusModelCurveCard` under a 'Temperature Compensation' heading at the foot of the Focus tab - it reads `focusProfileDataProvider`, so it is honest on the rig and on a paired companion alike, and it carries the chart, model quality/R2, prediction and per-filter offsets. Deleted the orphaned `focus_model_panel.dart` (973 lines, zero references, local-only data source that would have shown an empty model over the network) and corrected the stale comment in focus_model_settings.dart that named it. The finding's second half - 'clicking the TC chip in the status bar produced nothing' - is not a defect: status_bar/temperature_and_time.dart:71-95 is a Tooltip-wrapped Container, a passive badge whose tooltip already names slope, R2 and the predicted position; it was never a control, so no drill-in was lost. Mounting the model on Focus is the whole of the real gap.

title: Rotator relative-move strip clips +15 deg off the card with no scroll affordance
summary: Confirmed by measurement: at the 320 px imaging side panel the six step buttons laid out 16..432 inside a card that ends at 304, so +5 straddled the border and +15 sat entirely outside a clipped horizontal SingleChildScrollView with no fade or partial button to hint at it. Replaced the scroll strip with two rows of three Expanded cells (a fade would only have disclosed the problem, not fixed it): every step is drawn inside the card and hit-testable at any panel width, and the buttons get wider rather than narrower - which is what you want for a control you are tapping in the dark. Centred the button label since the box is now wider than its text.

title: Night Narrator ticker produced zero insights across a 65-minute session with 12 frames, an autofocus run and a cooldown
summary: Real, and the cause is structural rather than detector coverage. NarratorTicker returned SizedBox.shrink() whenever sessionStateProvider.dbSessionId was null - and only SequenceExecutor ever calls SessionStateNotifier.startSession, so every manual capture on the Imaging screen is sessionless. NarratorService deliberately keeps running in that case (it binds guiding, weather, autofocus and last-image-stats and persists events with a null session_id), but those rows only ever land in the sessionless bucket that the ticker never read. The strip is now fed from recentNarratorFeedProvider when there is no DB session, and the feed sheet it opens follows the same source so the two cannot contradict each other. The 10-minute rotation window is made mandatory in the sessionless case: that bucket outlives the app, so resting on its newest entry could put a previous night's headline over tonight's canvas.
